overall_note: The original recorded conclusion was PASS and is withdrawn. The recorded attempt's nine items all PASSED and are kept unchanged below; they simply did not cover what independent acceptance and code review then found. The unit conclusion is FAIL because (a) a P1 functional regression exists in the delivered unit, and (b) the cumulative full regression of the same candidate produced one unexplained required error.

withdrawn.by: independent acceptance and code review, not by the recorded attempt's own runner
withdrawn.consequence: G1b cannot close (M3 is the third of its three units) and G2a must not be treated as resting on an accepted baseline.

findings.summary: Read-back capacity was smaller than publication capacity. artifact-binding put the artifact body on the wire as base64, so a read request grew to about 4/3 of the artifact while every operation shares one fixed 8 MiB input ceiling. An artifact that put() accepted could therefore be unreadable, and an already published, already referenced artifact could not be read back at all.
findings.user_visible_consequence: Completed work could not be resumed: a worker that had written its receipt could not read it back on re-entry.
findings.reproduction: 6.25 MiB artifact: put() succeeds, the pre-migration get() succeeds, M3's get() raises 'bridge input exceeds 8 MiB'; a real worker re-entry fails.

findings.observed: The unchanged workflow test returned from the graph without a terminal key and raised KeyError('terminal') at line 54, with no check-complete, evaluate or seal before it.

classification.class: ESTABLISHED: a check-side runtime error surfaces through the check-runtime decision interrupt, so the graph returns with an interrupt and no terminal key. Reproduced deterministically by injecting a single fault (Store.job emits job-start then raises RuntimeBlocked), which yields an event signature identical to the retained log and the same KeyError.
classification.trigger_site: NOT RECOVERED. Three candidate sites (UNKNOWN_JOB, UNKNOWN_START, and the post-receipt Git validation in one_check) produce an identical observable signature, and the fixture deleted the job directory, so the retained evidence cannot distinguish them.
excluded_attributions: the M3 base64 capacity defect: the failure is at round 0, where one_check never reads a stored artifact

environment or timeout without evidence: the UNKNOWN_START budget is a fixed 10s while the measured supervisor startup to process.json is 38ms median (about 250x margin), and the observed suite slowdown was about 9x
classification.not_to_be_read_as: environmental noise, a proven new product defect, or the same base64 size defect

repair_candidate.p1_fix: artifact-binding now takes {ref, path}. Python keeps its own read_bytes() (preserving FileNotFoundError / IsADirectoryError) and Go verifies the bytes it reads at that same path, so a read request is a fixed-size envelope independent of the artifact. The 8 MiB ceiling is retained, not removed or widened.

acceptance_attempt.status: BLOCKED - 8 of 9 required items PASS; doctor-zcode cannot pass on this host. No record was issued.
acceptance_attempt.blocker: ZCODE_TRANSPORT: Native output closed (doctor exit 2). The ZCode app-server exits immediately.
acceptance_attempt.blocker_cause: SEE CORRECTION. The cause is not the host install. Two parts, both on our side: (a) FIXED - ZCode 3.12.3 ships the app-server's built-in provider catalogue at <Resources>/config/provider/zcode-builtin.json, while the app-server only derives <script dir>/provider/zcode-builtin.json and a source-tree-relative ../../../../../config/provider/zcode-builtin.json (which normalises to /config/provider/zcode-builtin.json). Both miss, so it exits 1 before emitting any protocol. The file is present; only its location moved. (b) NOT FIXED - the same build removed workspace/readState, which this transport calls first, and session/create now answers settings.model={"available": []} with no current selection.

attribution_withdrawn.was: M3-REPAIR-BLOCKED-BY-HOST-ZCODE: the host's ZCode install no longer ships the provider config, so this is not a product defect; unblock by installing a ZCode whose app-server starts.
attribution_withdrawn.why_wrong: "the artifact changed" was established (zcode.cjs e9f1868c/12615227 vs da61b066/11416833) but "therefore our side is fine" does not follow: the artifact changing is exactly what makes our assumption stale. Whether a defect is ours depends on whether our closed-world assumption about the host still holds, not on whether the host changed.
attribution_withdrawn.same_pattern_as: the already-retracted G2a attribution MODEL-ESCALATION-JUSTIFICATION-UNSUPPORTED - read the run's own evidence before attributing

acceptance_attempt.blocker_is_not_the_repair: Confirmed and unchanged: the identical launch failure reproduced on three candidates built separately in their own worktrees - d71113e (the M3 candidate on which this same check PASSED), c4bac49 (pre-repair) and 9e4a622 (repaired). The Go repair (f136303) and the Go supervisor are still not involved.

fix_applied.what: native_zcode.capture_binding() names the bundled catalogue through ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE - the host's own documented input for it - only when the host's own two candidates are absent, so a host whose lookup works is untouched. No file is written to the application bundle or to ~/.zcode. The catalogue is deliberately not added to the binding's file proofs, because the host refreshes it on its own.
fix_applied.verified: baseline: exit 1, no protocol emitted; with the catalogue named: alive and five startup/storageState events emitted. Point sensitivity: 3 of 4 new tests fail with the implementation reverted, 4/4 pass with it. go vet exit 0; Python suite 199 OK (195 before + 4 new).
fix_applied.effect_on_the_item: moves the failure forward, it does not clear it: ./scripts/harness doctor --provider zcode now answers {"ok": false, "error": "ZCODE_NATIVE workspace/readState: {\"code\": -32601, \"message\": \"Method not found: workspace/readState\"}"} instead of exiting at launch.

remaining_adaptation.what: The ZCode app-server protocol surface changed. workspace/readState is gone (0 occurrences in the 3.12.3 bundle; a call returns -32601) and session/create returns settings.model={"available": []} with no current for a fresh workspace, while selection() requires current. Neither is a rename: it is not known yet which call exposes the workspace's native model selection, and whether a workspace must be trusted first (workspace/hooks/trustGrant exists in the method table) was not determined. Excluded on evidence: our documented session/requestRuntimePreferences fallback answer is not what empties the catalogue - answering with an empty result instead yields model=null, also without current.
remaining_adaptation.why_not_fixed_here: It changes the transport's call sequence and model determination, which section 12.2 keeps out of the current unit and section 13.1 assigns to G2c (ZCode thin adapter).
remaining_adaptation.impact: doctor-zcode is one of the nine required items for EVERY unit, so no unit can close until this adaptation is done or a ZCode build speaking the previous surface is installed.

acceptance_attempt.disposition: The repair candidate stays UNACCEPTED. doctor-zcode is required and had always passed here, so it is not relabelled NOT_APPLICABLE and the missing result is not read as PASS. The recorded 8/9 stands as recorded. Unblocking condition: the G2c-scope adaptation above, or a ZCode build whose app-server speaks the previous surface.
